 now 17.26 EDT 62 mins: Dowman fails to thread a ball through the red shirts in front of them, and is then penalised for bringing down goalscorer Loupalo-Bi.
 Share 2m ago 17.24 EDT “That goal exemplifies why Gyokeres is so important for us,” writes Chris Lambert. “Yes it was trash, but we haven’t had a player for decades who gets in the space to score that kind of goal.” Decades? How quickly we forgot Lord Bendtner.
 Share 3m ago 17.23 EDT 60 mins: Dowman and Havertz almost link up inside the area, but Fleetwood clear upfield. Ched Evans is up against two defenders, though, and can’t hold the ball up for any length of time.
 Share 4m ago 17.22 EDT 58 mins: It’s going to be a long final half-four for Fleetwood, now struggling to get out of their own half. Havertz finds space again, meeting Odegaard’s clever cross and rifling the ball into the side netting.
 Share 6m ago 17.20 EDT 55 mins: Lynch parries Dowman’s cross into the path of Havertz, who has the goal at his mercy – but his shot clips the top of Bennett’s dome, and flies over the bar. A brilliant, if possibly unintentional clearance.
 Share 8m ago 17.17 EDT 52 mins: Fleetwood’s Crispin McLean is the first man in the book, and then blasts the ball downfield to nobody in particular as Arsenal turn the screw.
 Share Updated at  17.18 EDT 10m ago 17.16 EDT The goal was created by Ceadach O’Neill, who collected Hincapie’s long pass and threaded a cross towards Gyokeres. He tussled with Potter and clipped the ball as he went over, nudging it beyond the wrong-footed Lynch to level things up.
 View image in fullscreen A scrappy goal puts Arsenal level, no doubt Viktor Gyökeres will state that they all count. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Gyökeres celebrates in trademark fashion. Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images Share Updated at  17.26 EDT 12m ago 17.13 EDT GOAL! Fleetwood Town 1-1 Arsenal (Gyokeres 49')
 It’s about as scrappy a goal as you could imagine, but a very welcome one for Viktor Gyokeres, and for Arsenal .
 Share 13m ago 17.12 EDT Bradford 2-0 Peterborough: Adam Phillips finds the top corner, and the Bantams are closing in on the quarter-finals.
 Share 15m ago 17.10 EDT Second half
 Hincapie clears the ball away under pressure from Evans as we get back under way. I’m a little surprised that both Havertz and Gyokeres are still out there.
 Share 17m ago 17.08 EDT Arsenal changes: Ben White replaces Jurrien Timber, while captain Martin Ødegaard is on for Marli Salmon. A change of shape from Mikel Arteta, by the looks.
 Share 20m ago 17.05 EDT Half-time emails: 
 “Can I please register my total disgust that a lower league ground is hosting a top flight team in October on a grass pitch, and no one appears to have any mud on them. What are the fantastic grounds people at Fleetwood thinking?” – Nick Trim.
 “Where has Kepa’s career meandered that he now finds himself on the bench in a game against Fleetwood? Is Meslier really a better keeper than him? Meslier always appeared to be super shaky at Leeds” – Tony Hughes.
 “I can’t see Ceadach O’Neill emulating his Uncle Eoin’s antics in Windsor Park tonight. Not in this wind” – Justin Kavanagh.
 Share Updated at  17.06 EDT 31m ago 16.54 EDT Half time: Fleetwood Town 1-0 Arsenal
 The whistle blows and League Two’s Fleetwood lead the champions at half-time – and it’s hard to argue they don’t deserve it. Arsenal need to wake up.
 Share 33m ago 16.52 EDT 52 mins: O’Neill delivers an excellent cross to Timber at the far post, but Batty gets his face between ball and goal. Arsenal corner, but it comes to nothing …
 View image in fullscreen Arsenal's Jurrien Timber effort is blocked by Fleetwood Town's Jake Batty (right). Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  16.57 EDT 34m ago 16.51 EDT 50 mins: Dowman lifts a free kick into the area which nobody in navy blue can get a decisive touch on.
 Share 35m ago 16.50 EDT 48 mins: Fleetwood’s long-throw taker, Jake Batty, races back to take the ball away from Gyokeres. The home crowd give their verdict on Arsenal’s performance so far, in the form of a sweary chant.
 Share 37m ago 16.48 EDT 47 mins: From a Fleetwood throw, Lewis-Skelly and Salmon get mixed up and Meslier has to scurry out and clear it. The keeper is able to collect the next long throw with a degree of comfort.
 Share 39m ago 16.46 EDT 46 mins: Seven minutes of first-half stoppage time, as we get our first look at Arsenal’s superstar subs shivering on the bench.
 Share 40m ago 16.45 EDT 45 mins: Hincapie gets forward again and finds Dowman, but every Fleetwood player is back inside the penalty area, and there’s nowhere to go.
 Share 41m ago 16.45 EDT 44 mins: Approaching stoppage time in the first half, but there will be a fair bit after the long drone stoppage.
 Share 42m ago 16.43 EDT 42 mins: Hincapie curls in a tempting cross from the very corner of the penalty area – but it’s not tempting enough for Havertz or Gyokeres to get away from their markers.
 Share 44m ago 16.42 EDT It’s half-time in tonight’s other tie, with Bradford leading Peterborough 1-0 through Macaulay Gillesphey’s opener.
 Share 45m ago 16.41 EDT 39 mins: Kai Havertz, who has had less screen time than that distant drone, meets Dowman’s cross with a header, but skews it over the bar.
 Share 46m ago 16.40 EDT 38 mins: Lewis-Skelly finds Timber in the area and the ball ricochets to Dowman, whose cross has to be cleared away from danger.
 Share 47m ago 16.39 EDT 37 mins: Fleetwood centre-back Shaun Rooney (no relation) is a big aerial threat – while at St Johnstone, he scored the winner in two Cup finals in the same season. He’s pushing forward whenever the hosts have a chance to get upfield.
 Share 48m ago 16.37 EDT 36 mins: A spell of lukewarm Arsenal pressure is ended as Fleetwood get a free kick, allowing keeper Lynch to heave the ball clear.
 Share 50m ago 16.36 EDT 34 mins: After a spell of Arsenal possession, O’Neill cuts inside and thwacks it towards the danger area, but Harrison Neal is in place to block it away.
 Share 51m ago 16.34 EDT 33 mins: Northern Ireland manager Michael O’Neill is here, casting an eye over Fleetwood’s Conor Haughey and namesake Ceadach of Arsenal .
 Share 52m ago 16.34 EDT 32 mins: Dowman prods the ball past Haughey but can’t keep it from rolling out for a goal kick.
 Share 53m ago 16.32 EDT I guess Marli Salmon heard Arteta’s ‘Give me a headache, give me a problem’ request,” honks Andrew Schultz.
 Share 54m ago 16.32 EDT 31 mins: O’Neill takes the Arsenal corner and swings it towards Havertz, but Bennett is able to head away from danger.
 Share 55m ago 16.31 EDT 29 mins: Gyokeres has a go from 20 yards that’s on target, but easy for Cods keeper Jay Lynch to get down and gather.
 View image in fullscreen Viktor Gyokeres is unable to find an equaliser for the visitors. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.47 EDT 1h ago 16.29 EDT 27 mins: Arsenal are pushing forward but that inevitably leaves gaps in behind, and Evans is almost in the right place to latch on to a through ball.
 Share 1h ago 16.27 EDT 24 mins: Arsenal can’t make anything happen with a scrappy bit of possession in the Fleetwood area, and then Hincapie hoofs a clearance into the car park. Safe to say Arteta’s side haven’t settled.
 Share 1h ago 16.24 EDT Marli Salmon won’t want to watch that back; he let Loupalo-Bi get beyond him and his attempted late tackle only pushed the ball further away, allowing the striker to drill it clinically past Meslier. Sweet Carabao!
 View image in fullscreen Fleetwood Town’s Aaron Loupalo-Bi scores their first goal past Arsenal’s Illan Meslier. Photograph: Jon Super/Reuters View image in fullscreen Loupalo-Bi celebrates his fine finish. Photograph: Lewis Storey/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.34 EDT 1h ago 16.22 EDT GOAL! Fleetwood Town 1-0 Arsenal (Loupalo-Bi 20')
 Fourth-tier Fleetwood take the lead!! It’s Fulham loanee Aaron Loupalo-Bi with the opener, and Highbury goes wild!
 View image in fullscreen Scenes. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.31 EDT 1h ago 16.21 EDT 18 mins: A first opening for Arsenal on the break as Dowman crosses to Gyokeres, who can’t prod the ball home under pressure. And then …
 Share 1h ago 16.19 EDT “Good to see Ceadach O’Neill starting. His two uncles (Paddy & Eoin Bradley) were top class GAA players for Derry,” writes John Brennan. “Eoin was also a top player in the Irish League, winning a few cups along with getting a six-game ban for urinating in Windsor Park during a televised cup semi-final.” Well, that took a turn.
 Share 1h ago 16.18 EDT 15 mins: THUNK! After nice buildup work from Dowman, Lewis-Skelly goes for a 50-50 with Rooney but the Fleetwood defender prevails, and the thud of the challenge could probably be heard in Blackpool.
 Share 1h ago 16.16 EDT 14 mins: Another Fleetwood long throw aimed towards veteran forward Ched Evans, and mopped up by Meslier at the far post.
 View image in fullscreen Arsenal keeper Illan Meslier pounces on the ball. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock Share Updated at  16.22 EDT 1h ago 16.13 EDT 12 mins: Fleetwood launch a long throw into the danger area, where it’s flicked on by Bennett – but Arsenal get it clear.
 Share 1h ago 16.11 EDT We're back under way
 The drone has now disappeared, so the referee opts to restart. There are also murky reports of the culprit being apprehended by police. So, it’s back to the game, which will have at least eight minutes added to the first half.
 Share 1h ago 16.08 EDT “Who’s the wanker with the drone?” bellow the 5,000-strong home faithful, while the referee talks to Mikel Arteta, Matt Lawlor and various security staff. And now he’s waving the players back to the tunnel!
 Share 1h ago 16.04 EDT Drone delay!
 Arsenal get upfield early on and have a free kick … but play is suspended as the referee, Michael Salisbury, peers up at a distant light in the sky. There’s a drone hovering over Highbury, and it’ll need to be dealt with somehow.
 View image in fullscreen The culprit of the delay. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.09 EDT 1h ago 16.02 EDT On grounds with the same(ish) name, Tim Gutteridge writes: “I give you Liverpool (Anfield) and Stirling Albion who, until 1993, played their home games at Annfield (with an extra N).”
 “The similarities don’t stop there. For much of their history, Stirling Albion played in an all-red strip. And between 1970 and 1973 they were managed by Bob Shankly, the older brother of Liverpool’s Bill.”
 Share Updated at  16.02 EDT 1h ago 16.01 EDT First half
 Arsenal kick off, in their navy away threads with red and yellow strip. Fleetwood’s home kit is an Arsenal-esque red number with white sleeves.
 Share 1h ago 15.58 EDT The players are out on the pitch, in a fug of firework smoke after some very rapid-fire pyro greeted their arrival. Peter Drury, never knowingly understated, is the Sky commentator and is already talking nights with the stars, marble halls and “two teams galaxies apart”. Let’s go!
 View image in fullscreen Fireworks greet the players as they take to the pitch … Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images View image in fullscreen And smoke surrounds them as they line up. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.20 EDT 1h ago 15.56 EDT “I like to root for the underdog, so fingers crossed the Fishermen of the Cod Army will catch a really big one today!” cheers Peter Oh. It may interest you, Peter, that Fleetwood have a sub called Andy Cannon – surely destined to come on and sink the Gunners.
 View image in fullscreen Some fishy stickers inside Highbury. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.10 EDT 2h ago 15.54 EDT “‘Arsenal have paid us a lot of respect by naming such a strong team’?Not sure why Matt Lawlor’s being so polite, Arteta’s taking the proverbial Michael with that side. Three kids and a goalie on debut?” writes Dave Estherby. To be fair, one of those kids is Max Dowman, and there are a few first-team regulars in there.
 Share 2h ago 15.34 EDT Here’s the Fleetwood head coach, Matt Lawlor: “We’ve had to make changes, with the champions in town. But we’ve got a plan with substitutions to manage the game. Arsenal have paid us a lot of respect by naming such a strong team … it’s a very difficult challenge, but one we should enjoy, and not be overawed.”
 Share 2h ago 15.32 EDT “I was just thinking, with the two Highburys – I can only think of the St James(’) Parks (Exeter and Newcastle), but are there any other grounds with very similar names?” asks Shaun T.
 Share 2h ago 15.25 EDT “It’s very special, coming to these kinds of grounds – it’s proper English football,” says Mikel Arteta. “In these kinds of conditions, you’re in or you’re out. It’s great to have Marli, Max and Ceadach with us, Ilhan Meslier as well who is making his first appearance for us.” His advice to those young Gunners? “Give me a headache, give me a problem – give me a reason to play you.”
 View image in fullscreen Fleetwood Town fans do their bit to create a proper cup tie atmosphere. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA Share Updated at  16.05 EDT 2h ago 15.22 EDT There is one other fourth-round Carabao Cup tie tonight, and it’s an all-League One affair. Bradford City , finalists in 2013, host Robbie Savage’s Peterborough – guaranteeing that at least one third-tier side will make the quarter-finals. Like the match at Highbury, it will go to penalties if still level after 90 minutes – and there’s no VAR.
 View image in fullscreen Valley Parade under the lights. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA Share 2h ago 15.14 EDT So, Ilhan Meslier makes his debut in goal for Arsenal , with Christian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie starting as they return from injury; Martin Zubimendi also gets a run-out, while youngsters Max Dowman, Marli Salmon and Ceadach O’Neill all included in Mikel Arteta’s starting XI.
 Share 2h ago 15.06 EDT Team news
 Fleetwood Town (3-5-2): Lynch, Haughey, Potter, Bennett; Rooney, Neal, McLean, Helm, Batty; Evans, Loupalo-Bi.
 Subs: Pradic, Andrew, Cannon, Davies, Thomas, Murphy, Coughlan, Robertson, Cirino. 
 Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Meslier; Timber, Mosquera, Salmon, Hincapie; Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly; Dowman, Havertz, O’Neill; Gyokeres.
 Subs: Arrizabalaga, White, Odegaard, Eze, Konsa, Guimaraes, Hashi, Washington, Harriman-Annous. 
 Referee: Michael Salisbury (Lancashire)
 Share Updated at  15.17 EDT 2h ago 15.03 EDT Will Unwin To give everyone a flavour of conditions, it is blowing a gale around the rather quaint Highbury Stadium, almost blowing my laptop onto the pitch. Mikel Arteta will not be too worried about his players adapting to the conditions and will see a front pairing of Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres as integral to killing this game off as soon as possible.
 Fleetwood, however, are here to give the Gunners a bloody nose at the very least. They know how to utilise the conditions to their favour and will be straight into the faces of the Premier League champions. They may sit 18th in League Two, but they saw off Sheffield United in the last round and will fancy doing likewise in front of a packed ground.
 Share 2h ago 15.00 EDT Some sad news to bring you: Peter Dobing , the captain of Stoke’s 1972 League Cup winning side, has died at the age of 87.
 Dobing made 377 appearances over a decade with the Potters and also played for Blackburn and Manchester City. He captained Stoke to glory as they beat Chelsea 2-1 to clinch their first (and only) major trophy, before his playing career was ended by injury just one year later.
 Stoke said in a statement: “All at Stoke are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of our ’72 League Cup-winning captain Peter Dobing at the age of 87. The thoughts and sincere condolences of all are with Peter’s friends and family at this immensely difficult time.”
 View image in fullscreen Peter Dobing holds the League Cup aloft during the team’s parade in Stoke, with Gordon Banks to his left. Photograph: Jim Hutchison/ANL/Shutterstock Share 3h ago 14.53 EDT Some essential pre-match reading here from Will Unwin, our man on the Fylde coast tonight.
 ‘The wind goes in all directions’: Fleetwood prepare wet welcome for Arsenal at Highbury Read more Share Updated at  14.56 EDT 3h ago 14.30 EDT Preamble
 Some Arsenal fans spent years pining for one more game at Highbury Stadium; tonight, they finally get their wish. This particular Highbury is 250 miles northwest of Islington – the home of Fleetwood Town , a team the Gunners have never played before.
 While their League Two form could hardly be less remarkable (18th place, with 14 points from 13 games), Fleetwood have picked off Chesterfield, Shrewsbury and second-tier Sheffield United in the Carabao Cup without conceding a goal, earning a last-16 glamour tie against the English champions.
 With a trip to Anfield looming on Sunday, Mikel Arteta is expected to give his weariest stars a rest. Young talents like Marli Salmon, Ceadach O’Neill and, yes, Max Dowman are expected to start. They can expect testing conditions at a seaside ground where “the wind goes in all directions” .
 Of course, even a depleted and under-experienced Arsenal side will be hot favourites to advance, but this has all the makings of a classic midweek Cup test. Kick-off: 8pm GMT.
